section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the request for joy in Chochmah and Binah draws from a limitless essential joy beyond all boundaries, enabling a permanent inner union of Abba and Imma.
section.t: And this is, “Gladden the beloved companions,” that joy must be drawn into Chochmah and Binah,
even though the place of joy is in Binah,
and in Chochmah there is a delight that is above joy,
for the joy in Binah and the delight in Chochmah are
(analogous to)
the joy and delight that come from the revealed powers,
and consequently, they involve measure and limitation.
And although the innerness of Abba is the innerness of Atik,
and particularly since the intention is not only for the aspect of the innerness of Atik alone, but until the first root of the aspect of innerness and Atzmus of Ein Sof,
nevertheless, this matter pertains to the inner union of Abba and Imma,
and this union must be aroused and drawn down
(for the inner union of Abba and Imma is only intermittent).
And this is what we ask: “Gladden the beloved companions,”
that the essential joy be drawn into Chochmah and Binah
(and even from the innerness and Atzmus of Ein Sof)
which is entirely beyond the category of limitation,
a joy that breaks through all boundaries
(as above),
and through this, the inner union of Chochmah and Binah is effected,
and this union will also be a permanent union.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section states that the main purpose of the inner union of Chochmah and Binah is to bring about the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah, which is the primary vehicle for drawing down the Essence.
section.t: And the main intention in this
(in the inner union of Chochmah and Binah)
is so that through it there will be the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah,
“for this is the main thing.”
And as is explained at length in the maamar,
that specifically through the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah is the drawing down of the Essence,
therefore, specifically from the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah is a new creation effected
(the birth of souls),
except that in order for there to be the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah,
there must first be the inner union of Chochmah and Binah.
And this is “Gladden the beloved companions”
(“beloved” in gematria equals “dodim,”
Zeir Anpin and Nukvah),
for the request that there be a drawing of joy into Chochmah and Binah, through which there will be the inner union of Chochmah and Binah,
is for the sake of the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the request for essential joy to the joy of marriage, explaining that creation ex nihilo comes from the Essence, and through the mitzvah of procreation, this essential joy is drawn down.
section.t: And based on this, the connection of this request to the joy of marriage will also be understood.
For it is known
that the creation of yesh mei’ayin (something from nothing) is specifically through the power of the Essence.
For all lights and revelations,
since they have at least a cause or a reason,
are not capable of bringing into being a thing
(“yesh”)
that has no
(in its own perception)
cause or reason,
for it is impossible for any existent to influence what is not within its power,
and the coming into being of yesh is only through the power of the Essence, whose existence is from its very Self and has no cause or reason preceding it, G-d forbid.
Now, the “drawing down” of the Essence to create yesh mei’ayin
(during the six days of creation)
was because
“He desires kindness.”
But after the giving of the Torah, for this drawing down to occur, it is through the service of Torah and mitzvos,
and it can be said that specifically
(and in a revealed way)
it is through the mitzvos that are related to the matter of breaking boundaries,
such as the mitzvah of procreation,
as is known,
that in the matter of procreation
(to give birth generation after generation)
there is a revelation of the power of Ein Sof,
and particularly since the matter of procreation is
(also)
analogous to creation yesh mei’ayin,
which is through the power of the Essence.
And this is
what we request at a wedding: “Gladden the beloved companions,”
for the ultimate purpose of marriage is that there be procreation,
“Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth,”
and therefore we then request “Gladden the beloved companions,”
that there be a drawing down of the essential joy of the Essence of Ein Sof.
And this is also what we say
(in the continuation of the blessing)
“As You gladdened Your creation in the Garden of Eden of old,”
for the drawing down of joy in the Garden of Eden of old
(at the beginning of creation)
was because “He desires kindness.”
And we request that also now, through our service in Torah and mitzvos,
and particularly through the joy of marriage,
this drawing down should occur.
